interest: 1919 Manchurian tax dispute and 1936–38 Pan Am flights over the Japanese Mandate.
keywords: Foreign Relations of the United States
overview: This decimal file (894.0144, covering 1931-1938, with earlier 1919 records filed under 894.0144/26) documents matters of Japanese territorial sovereignty, extraterritorial jurisdiction, and airspace violations. The file comprises two distinct documentary groups: the first consists of 1919 diplomatic despatches and legal statements regarding the refusal of the United States to recognize the authority of the South Manchuria Railway Company to levy municipal income taxes on American citizens residing in the Japanese railway concession at Mukden, Manchuria, along with 1930s cross-reference sheets concerning clearance to publish these despatches in Foreign Relations of the United States. The second group (1936-1938) concerns Japanese diplomatic protests over reported violations of Japanese territorial airspace in the mandated Mariana Islands, specifically an incident where a Pan American Airways commercial flying boat under Captain Edwin Musick allegedly flew over the island of Rota en route between Midway and Guam, as well as an indexed 1938 overflight of the Ladrones.

subfiles.about: Cover sheet transmitting copies of 1919 correspondence regarding Japanese taxation in Manchuria for inclusion in the Foreign Relations documentary volume.
keywords: Foreign Relations of the United States
subfiles.summary: Transmittal slip for 1919 papers on Japanese taxing of Americans in Manchuria, compiled for Foreign Relations.
subfiles.title: State Department Transmittal Slip for 1919 Foreign Relations Correspondence

subfiles.about: Consular despatch reporting on the Japanese administration's attempts to levy an income tax on American residents in the railway concession at Mukden.
subfiles.from: E. Carleton Baker (American Consul General, Mukden)
subfiles.summary: Baker reports Japanese authorities in Mukden's railway concession taxing Americans' incomes, forwards his protest and the reply, and asks for instructions.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 229 from Baker (Mukden) on Japanese Attempt to Levy Tax on Americans

subfiles.about: Diplomatic letter protesting the legality of Japanese authorities levying an income tax on American residents in the Japanese settlement at Mukden.
subfiles.from: E. Carleton Baker (American Consul General, Mukden)
subfiles.summary: Baker protests to the Japanese Consul General that a salary-based income tax on Americans goes beyond municipal rates and is taxation without representation.
subfiles.title: Letter from Baker to Akatsuka Protesting Income Tax on Americans in Mukden

subfiles.about: Consular letter acknowledging the American protest and forwarding the South Manchuria Railway Company's formal legal position on taxation.
subfiles.summary: Akatsuka acknowledges Baker's protest and encloses the South Manchuria Railway Company's statement on the tax.
subfiles.title: Letter from Akatsuka to Baker Enclosing South Manchuria Railway Company Statement
subfiles.to: E. Carleton Baker (American Consul General, Mukden)

subfiles.about: Legal memorandum asserting the South Manchuria Railway Company's absolute administrative and taxing authority over all residents in the railway zone.
subfiles.from: President of the South Manchuria Railway Company
subfiles.summary: The South Manchuria Railway Company claims full authority in its zone and says residents' payments cover only about 6 percent of costs.
subfiles.title: Statement by the President of the South Manchuria Railway Company on Railway Zone Taxation

subfiles.about: State Department instruction rejecting the South Manchuria Railway Company's legal authority to levy political taxes on American citizens.
subfiles.from: Wilbur J. Carr (for the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: State rejects the railway company's claim, says it cannot tax Americans' incomes, and tells Baker that any payments are voluntary.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 77 to Baker (Mukden) on Japanese Taxation Rights in Manchuria
subfiles.to: E. Carleton Baker (American Consul General, Mukden)

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Publication of 1919 Foreign Relations Correspondence

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Publication of 1920 Foreign Relations Correspondence

subfiles.about: Letter from Pan American Airways explaining the navigation of a transpacific clipper flight near the Japanese-mandated island of Rota.
subfiles.from: John C. Cooper, Jr. (Vice President, Pan American Airways Company)
subfiles.summary: John C. Cooper, Jr. of Pan American explains that Captain Musick detoured around storms north of Rota in 1936 and believes he avoided the island.
subfiles.title: Letter from Pan American Airways on Alleged Flight over Rota

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum recording a conversation with Pan American Airways requesting a formal written explanation of the Rota flight.
subfiles.summary: Memo of a call with Pan American's J. H. Smith about Japan's protest over a 1936 flight over Rota.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Telephone Conference with Pan American Airways regarding Rota Overflight

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum detailing Japanese diplomatic inquiries and early State Department discussions regarding the flight over Rota.
subfiles.summary: Memo summarizing Japan's request to investigate a silver plane over Rota on October 26, 1936.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese Foreign Office Inquiry into Airplane Flight over Rota
subfiles.to: Richard Southgate (Chief, Division of Protocol and Conferences)

subfiles.about: Instruction directing Ambassador Grew to present Pan American Airways' formal explanation of the Rota overflight to the Japanese Foreign Office.
subfiles.from: H. Walton Moore (for the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 1351 sends Grew Pan American's explanation of Musick's 1936 detour near Rota.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1351 to Grew (Tokyo) Transmitting Pan American Explanation of Rota Flight

subfiles.about: Document file note referencing a telegram from Hong Kong concerning a Pan American plane flying over the Ladrones toward Macau.
